title: Nobel Prize Awarded to Economists for Stabilizing Global Markets
subtitle: Robert Hall and Michael Woodford recognized for tools that help central banks manage economic ups and downs

summary.en: Two American economists have been awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences. Robert Hall and Michael Woodford were honored for developing new models to manage economic crises. Their work, known as the 'New Keynesian' approach, helps governments control inflation and unemployment. The committee praised their research for providing a stable foundation for modern economic policy. This award highlights the importance of clear communication between central banks and the public.
summary.zh: 兩位美國經濟學家榮獲二〇二六年諾貝爾經濟學獎。霍爾與伍德福德因開發出管理經濟危機的新模型而獲獎。他們的研究被稱為「新凱因斯」途徑，有助於政府控制通貨膨脹與失業率。委員會讚揚他們的研究為現代經濟政策提供了穩定的基礎。此獎項凸顯了中央銀行與大眾之間進行清晰溝通的重要性。

paragraphs.en: Two American economists have been awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for their groundbreaking work in helping governments and central banks manage economic crises. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced that Robert Hall of Stanford University and Michael Woodford of Columbia University will share the prize, which is worth approximately $1.2 million. The award recognizes their role in creating a 'paradigm shift'—a major change in how experts understand and manage the economy.
paragraphs.zh: 兩位美國經濟學家因其在協助政府與中央銀行管理經濟危機方面的開創性貢獻，榮獲二〇二六年諾貝爾經濟學獎。瑞典皇家科學院宣布，史丹佛大學的霍爾（Robert Hall）與哥倫比亞大學的伍德福德（Michael Woodford）將共同分享這筆約一百二十萬美元的獎金。該獎項旨在表彰他們在創造「典範轉移」——即專家理解與管理經濟方式的重大變革——中所扮演的角色。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian Business, the researchers were honored for developing the 'microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation.' In simpler terms, they created tools that help policymakers smooth out the 'peaks and troughs' of the economy. These tools allow central banks to avoid long periods of recession and runaway inflation, which is when prices for goods and services rise very quickly, making money worth less.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》商業版報導，這兩位研究人員因發展出「總體經濟穩定化的個體經濟基礎」而獲獎。簡單來說，他們創造了能協助決策者平抑經濟「高峰與低谷」的工具。這些工具讓中央銀行得以避免長期的經濟衰退與惡性通貨膨脹，後者指的是商品與服務價格快速上漲，導致貨幣價值縮水的現象。

paragraphs.en: This new research was necessary because older methods, developed by John Maynard Keynes almost a century ago, struggled to handle the economic shocks of the 1970s. During that time, many countries suffered from high unemployment, low growth, and high inflation all at once. NPR News reports that committee member Tim Boppart described the old 'Keynesian recipe' as being 'shattered' by these events. Hall and Woodford provided the missing ingredients by focusing on how individual households and businesses make decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 這項新研究之所以必要，是因為約一世紀前由凱因斯（John Maynard Keynes）所發展出的舊有方法，難以應對一九七〇年代的經濟衝擊。當時，許多國家同時面臨高失業率、低成長與高通貨膨脹的困境。美國公共廣播電台報導，委員會成員波帕特（Tim Boppart）形容舊有的「凱因斯處方」已被這些事件「粉碎」。霍爾與伍德福德透過聚焦於個別家庭與企業如何做出決策，補足了缺失的環節。

paragraphs.en: Unlike older, more mechanical models, the work of Hall and Woodford looks at how people think about the future. Hall’s research focused on how families decide to spend money based on what they expect their future income to be. If people feel worried about the future, they start saving money and spending less today. Meanwhile, Woodford focused on how businesses set their prices. Because it is often expensive or difficult to change prices frequently, businesses try to look ahead and set prices that will cover their costs for a long time. By understanding these behaviors, central banks can better predict how the economy will react to different policies.
paragraphs.zh: 與較舊且較機械化的模型不同，霍爾與伍德福德的研究探討了人們如何思考未來。霍爾的研究聚焦於家庭如何根據對未來收入的預期來決定消費。如果人們對未來感到擔憂，他們就會開始儲蓄並減少當前的支出。與此同時，伍德福德則專注於企業如何制定價格。由於頻繁調整價格通常成本高昂或困難重重，企業會試圖展望未來，制定能長期涵蓋其成本的價格。透過理解這些行為，中央銀行能更準確地預測經濟將如何對不同政策做出反應。

paragraphs.en: One of the most important results of their work is a tool called 'forward guidance.' This is a method where central bankers communicate their future plans for interest rates—the cost of borrowing money—to the public. By being clear about their goals, policymakers can influence how people and businesses act. Woodford told reporters that government authorities should not just pull levers to control the economy in secret. Instead, he argued that stabilization works much better when the public understands what the government is trying to accomplish and why.
paragraphs.zh: 他們研究最重要的成果之一是名為「前瞻指引」的工具。這是一種中央銀行向大眾溝通其未來利率（借貸成本）計畫的方法。透過明確說明目標，決策者可以影響個人與企業的行為。伍德福德告訴記者，政府當局不應只是在幕後操作槓桿來控制經濟。相反地，他主張當大眾理解政府試圖達成什麼目標及其原因時，穩定化措施的效果會好得多。

paragraphs.en: Despite its success, this approach has faced some criticism. The Guardian Business noted that some experts worry about the risks of clear communication. For example, Kevin Warsh, the current chair of the US Federal Reserve, has argued that forward guidance should have a limited role to avoid creating confusion. In the past, officials like former Bank of England governor Mark Carney were even criticized for dropping hints about future interest rate changes that never actually happened.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管取得了成功，這種方法也面臨一些批評。《衛報》商業版指出，一些專家擔心清晰溝通所帶來的風險。例如，現任美國聯邦準備理事會主席沃爾什（Kevin Warsh）曾主張，前瞻指引的角色應受到限制，以避免造成混亂。過去，像前英格蘭銀行總裁卡尼（Mark Carney）這樣的官員，甚至曾因暗示未來利率變動卻最終未實現而受到批評。

paragraphs.en: Nevertheless, the Nobel committee emphasized that the work of Hall and Woodford has been essential in recent years. Their models were used extensively after the 2008 financial crisis to prevent a second Great Depression. More recently, these tools helped governments navigate the economic challenges caused by the Covid-19 pandemic and global supply chain issues. John Hassler, the chair of the committee for the economics prize, stated that the laureates have provided a stable foundation that makes the world better equipped to deal with energy crises and sudden changes in consumer behavior.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管如此，諾貝爾委員會強調，霍爾與伍德福德的研究在近年來至關重要。他們的研究模型在二〇〇八年金融危機後被廣泛使用，以防止第二次經濟大蕭條。近期，這些工具協助政府應對由新冠肺炎疫情與全球供應鏈問題所引發的經濟挑戰。經濟學獎委員會主席哈斯勒（John Hassler）表示，獲獎者提供了一個穩定的基礎，使世界更有能力應對能源危機與消費者行為的突發性改變。

paragraphs.en: While the economics prize is formally known as the Bank of Sweden Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel, it is always presented alongside the other Nobel Prizes on December 10, the anniversary of Alfred Nobel’s death. This year’s recognition of Hall and Woodford underscores the ongoing effort to make the global economy more predictable and stable for everyone. As Woodford said after receiving the news, he felt 'elated' and called the award a 'tremendous honour.'
paragraphs.zh: 雖然經濟學獎正式名稱為「瑞典國家銀行紀念阿爾弗雷德·諾貝爾經濟學獎」，但它總是在阿爾弗雷德·諾貝爾逝世週年紀念日的十二月十日，與其他諾貝爾獎一同頒發。今年對霍爾與伍德福德的表彰，凸顯了讓全球經濟對所有人而言更具可預測性與穩定性的持續努力。正如伍德福德在獲知消息後所言，他感到「欣喜若狂」，並稱該獎項為「巨大的榮譽」。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To make something less extreme or to reduce the severity of fluctuations.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於描述表面平滑，這裡指減少經濟波動。文中：In simpler terms, they created tools that help policymakers smooth out the 'peaks and troughs' of the economy.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To use the mechanisms or tools of power to influence a system.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 運用手段或權力來操控系統。
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意思是拉動槓桿，這裡比喻政府操控經濟政策。文中：Woodford told reporters that government authorities should not just pull levers to control the economy in secret.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To mention something indirectly or hint at it.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見指「掉落」，這裡指「透露」訊息。文中：In the past, officials like former Bank of England governor Mark Carney were even criticized for dropping hints about future interest rate changes that never actually happened.

previousArticles.summaryEn: Two American economists, Robert Hall and Michael Woodford, have won the 2026 Nobel Prize in economics. Their research created the 'New Keynesian' model, which helps central banks manage inflation and unemployment. By focusing on how families and businesses make decisions, their work provides a foundation for modern economic policy. The prize committee noted that these tools were essential during the 2008 financial crisis and the recent pandemic. While their methods are widely used, some experts continue to debate the best ways to communicate these policies to the public.

quiz.question: According to the article, why did the 'Keynesian recipe' become insufficient for managing the economy?

options.A: It failed to account for the role of central banks in setting interest rates.
options.B: It could not effectively address the combination of high unemployment and high inflation seen in the 1970s.
options.C: It relied too heavily on the decisions of individual households rather than government policies.
options.D: It was based on outdated information from the 2008 financial crisis.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第三段明確指出，約翰·梅納德·凱因斯（Keynes）的方法在處理 1970 年代的經濟衝擊時遇到了困難，當時各國同時面臨高失業率、低成長與高通貨膨脹。選項 A 錯誤，因為凱因斯理論並非忽略央行。選項 C 錯誤，因為凱因斯方法被認為過於機械化，缺乏對個體決策的關注。選項 D 時間點錯誤，1970 年代的危機遠早於 2008 年金融危機。

quiz.question: Based on the description of 'forward guidance,' what can be inferred about the relationship between public communication and economic stability?

options.A: Economic stability is best achieved when central banks keep their future interest rate plans secret.
options.B: Public communication is always effective at preventing economic recessions.
options.C: Transparency about future policies can influence the current behavior of households and businesses.
options.D: Central bankers should avoid communicating with the public to prevent market confusion.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第五段，前瞻指引（forward guidance）透過公開未來利率計畫來影響公眾與企業的行為。這顯示透明度能作為一種政策工具，透過改變人們的預期來穩定經濟。選項 A 與文章觀點相反。選項 B 過於絕對，文章僅提到這是一種工具，並非萬靈丹。選項 D 雖然提到有人擔心溝通會造成混亂，但這並非該工具的主要目的或推論出的結論。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, the word 'elated' is used to describe how Michael Woodford felt. What does this word mean in context?

options.B: Confused by the complexity of the award.
options.C: Relieved that the work is finally finished.
options.D: Worried about the responsibility of the prize.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在最後一段中，Woodford 說他感到「elated」並稱該獎項為「巨大的榮譽」（tremendous honour）。從語境判斷，這是在描述獲得諾貝爾獎後的正面情緒，因此意指極度高興與自豪。選項 B、C、D 皆為負面或中性的情緒，與獲得重大榮譽時的語境不符。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding the work of Hall and Woodford?

options.A: They successfully replaced all older economic theories with a single, perfect model.
options.B: Their research has provided a new, behavior-based framework that helps governments better navigate modern economic crises.
options.C: Their primary contribution was identifying the specific causes of the 2008 financial crisis.
options.D: They are the first economists to argue that central banks should have no role in managing the economy.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。全文重點在於介紹兩位經濟學家如何透過將個體行為（家庭與企業決策）納入宏觀經濟模型，創造了新的穩定工具，並在 2008 年危機與疫情期間發揮了關鍵作用。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章提到這是「paradigm shift」，而非完全取代所有理論。選項 C 錯誤，2008 年僅是其模型應用的一個例子，而非唯一貢獻。選項 D 與文章內容完全相反，他們的研究正是為了強化央行的管理能力。
